title: Investigating the learning patterns of participants with public speaking anxiety and social anxiety disorder using a fear conditioning paradigm
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate differences in fear learning processes between individuals with public speaking anxiety and healthy controls  (Study 1).
Participants with moderate to severe public speaking anxiety (with or without social anxiety disorder) will complete an online fear conditioning experiment (Labvanced), consisting of acquisition, generalization, and extinction phases. Neutral faces serve as conditioned stimuli (CS+ / CS−), and a video serves as the aversive stimulus (US). US-expectancy ratings are collected throughout all phases.
The data will be compared with datasets from healthy participants who completed the same experiment, to analyze group differences in fear learning. 
In a further step (Study 2), it will be examined whether these patterns of fear processing are related to how individuals with PSA respond to exposure-based exercises targeting public speaking anxiety.

Inclusion criteria:
Fluent in German
For group with PSA and/or SAD:

Exclusion criteria:
For group with PSA and/or SAD:
- Individuals with current mental disorders other than public speaking anxiety and/or social anxiety disorder are excluded from participation. Individuals meeting criteria for social anxiety disorder are eligible to participate.
